outline.title: 视觉自监督表示学习中的对比与非对比方法综述

sections.title: 引言
keyPoints: 界定视觉自监督表示学习的综述范围：基于负样本的对比方法与无负样本的孪生方法两条路线；材料为四篇公开摘要，没有本文实验。

sections.title: 基于负样本的对比框架
keyPoints: 解释 SimCLR 的数据增强组合、可学习非线性变换与大批量长训练三项发现，以及 MoCo 以队列和动量编码器构建大而一致的动态字典。

sections.title: 无负样本的孪生方法
keyPoints: 解释 BYOL 以在线网络预测目标网络表示并用慢速移动平均更新目标网络，以及 SimSiam 不用负样本、大批量和动量编码器而依靠停止梯度防止坍缩。

sections.title: 综合比较与局限性
keyPoints: 沿负样本依赖、批量规模依赖、目标编码器更新方式与防坍缩机制比较两条路线；摘要数值来自不同模型与评测设置，不能据此给出性能排序；材料仅四篇摘要，未统一复现。

sections.title: 结论与展望
keyPoints: 总结两条路线的关系与各自改变的训练要素，保留限制；统一协议下的评测是未来工作而非已完成贡献。

source.title: A Simple Framework for Contrastive Learning of Visual Representations

evidence.claim: This paper presents SimCLR: a simple framework for contrastive learning of visual representations. We simplify recently proposed contrastive self-supervised learning algorithms without requiring specialized architectures or a memory bank.

source.title: A Simple Framework for Contrastive Learning of Visual Representations

evidence.claim: We show that (1) composition of data augmentations plays a critical role in defining effective predictive tasks, (2) introducing a learnable nonlinear transformation between the representation and the contrastive loss substantially improves the quality of the learned representations, and (3) contrastive learning benefits from larger batch sizes and more training steps compared to supervised learning.

source.title: A Simple Framework for Contrastive Learning of Visual Representations

evidence.claim: A linear classifier trained on self-supervised representations learned by SimCLR achieves 76.5% top-1 accuracy, which is a 7% relative improvement over previous state-of-the-art, matching the performance of a supervised ResNet-50. When fine-tuned on only 1% of the labels, we achieve 85.8% top-5 accuracy, outperforming AlexNet with 100X fewer labels.

source.title: Momentum Contrast for Unsupervised Visual Representation Learning

evidence.claim: We present Momentum Contrast (MoCo) for unsupervised visual representation learning. From a perspective on contrastive learning as dictionary look-up, we build a dynamic dictionary with a queue and a moving-averaged encoder. This enables building a large and consistent dictionary on-the-fly that facilitates contrastive unsupervised learning.

source.title: Momentum Contrast for Unsupervised Visual Representation Learning

evidence.claim: MoCo provides competitive results under the common linear protocol on ImageNet classification. More importantly, the representations learned by MoCo transfer well to downstream tasks. MoCo can outperform its supervised pre-training counterpart in 7 detection/segmentation tasks on PASCAL VOC, COCO, and other datasets, sometimes surpassing it by large margins.

source.title: Bootstrap your own latent: A new approach to self-supervised Learning

evidence.claim: BYOL relies on two neural networks, referred to as online and target networks, that interact and learn from each other. From an augmented view of an image, we train the online network to predict the target network representation of the same image under a different augmented view. At the same time, we update the target network with a slow-moving average of the online network.

source.title: Bootstrap your own latent: A new approach to self-supervised Learning

evidence.claim: While state-of-the art methods rely on negative pairs, BYOL achieves a new state of the art without them. BYOL reaches $74.3\%$ top-1 classification accuracy on ImageNet using a linear evaluation with a ResNet-50 architecture and $79.6\%$ with a larger ResNet. We show that BYOL performs on par or better than the current state of the art on both transfer and semi-supervised benchmarks.

evidence.claim: Siamese networks have become a common structure in various recent models for unsupervised visual representation learning. These models maximize the similarity between two augmentations of one image, subject to certain conditions for avoiding collapsing solutions.

evidence.claim: In this paper, we report surprising empirical results that simple Siamese networks can learn meaningful representations even using none of the following: (i) negative sample pairs, (ii) large batches, (iii) momentum encoders. Our experiments show that collapsing solutions do exist for the loss and structure, but a stop-gradient operation plays an essential role in preventing collapsing.
